note: GSTA-152 plan item 8. Per-meter constants for /ship budget projections, fitted conservatively from metered runs: each constant is the largest observation times `headroom`, rounded up to `round_to` (lib/ship-budget.ts fitConstant). test/ship-budget-calibration.test.ts checks the constants equal the fit and that a leave-one-out fit on two runs is at or above the meter on the third. Savings claims count completed ships only. Each unit's call_floor (GSTA-167) is the host's per-call floor: what one call costs in a fresh session with the ship skill loaded, before any /ship work. The delegate thresholds compare the per-call charge minus this floor, so a host's own system prompt and tools never trigger delegation. A floor is the largest round_to multiple at or below its smallest observed fresh call, so it never hides real context growth; start --call-floor <n> overrides it for one run. Step priors (GSTA-167 round 3): a step holds only its own calls; each audit dispatch (Steps 7, 8, 14.5) is reserved by its own check, so it moved from step_dispatches to segment_dispatches, where a child's segment estimate still counts it. On the Capy meter a step is priced at step_calls x the run's own median measured per-call charge once three calls are measured (lib/ship-budget.ts measuredPerCall), and at per_call before that. A keyed step_calls entry is the ceiling of the most calls step_calls_observed holds for it, and an unkeyed step's observations stay at or below default. Each observation is a step window's measured actual (step samples in the round-3 replay ledgers mirrored under the project-user Drive folder ship-budget/) divided by 330k, the per-call charge replay3-34.md reports for gstack-evals #34; replay3-36.md reports no per-call figure, so #36 uses the same 330k. Steps 7 and 9 have no step measurement yet and keep 12. The #3633 lane's first ledger (ship-20261030T020246-7c4b65) read the root counter, which holds sibling threads, so its step samples are left out.

capy-tokens.call_floor_why: GSTA-2 (gstack 1.91.320.0, gstack-evals #35/#36): a fresh Capy thread's first counter reading is about 98k (host system prompt and tools) and every call with the ship skill loaded costs 150-230k before any /ship work; 150k is the smallest observed call. estimate-tokens.why: the estimate meter projects with the Capy fit, which is at or above the meter on the metered runs
estimate-tokens.call_floor_why: The estimate meter takes no readings, so its per-call charge is always unknown and the floor has nothing to subtract: an unknown charge keeps the pre-floor rule (delegate at a segment boundary, never at start).
